neighbours.label: the predicate slot after an indefinite 'a(n) N for/to X' subject whose existence or availability is at issue (A method for … ▁is still lacking / ▁was needed / ▁has not been found); the output promotes ' exists', ' available'
fire: A convincing account of how the tunnel collapsed is not yet available.
A cheap way of storing the surplus grain was urgently required.
A vaccine for the new strain has yet to be developed.
A satisfactory solution to the parking problem does not exist.
An accurate map of the northern coast was badly needed by the fleet.
A practical test for detecting the toxin is still missing.
A proper legal framework for drone deliveries has not emerged.
An agreed standard for labelling the samples is lacking.
quiet: The official account of how the tunnel collapsed is forty pages long.
The old way of storing the surplus grain was cheap and simple.
The vaccine for the new strain has two doses.
The mayor's solution to the parking problem does annoy the shopkeepers.
The fleet's map of the northern coast was drawn in 1802.
The nurse from the clinic is still asleep.
My cousin in the legal department has a new drone.
The girl who labelled the samples is my sister.

notes: Card: ' is' x11, ' was' x5, ' has' after subjects like 'a clear answer to this question', 'a method for transporting these guns', 'an explanation for this'; + pole reverses toward exists/available. Probes: indefinite subjects 0.80-0.98; definite 'The explanation for … is' 0.25, 'The method for … was' 0.16, 'No evidence of fraud was' 0.23, 'My brother is' 0.00.
